newsitem.title: USA: Columbus gets anti-trust regulatory okay.
newsitem.headline: Columbus gets anti-trust regulatory okay.

text.p: Columbus McKinnon Corp received anti-trust regulatory clearance for its bid to acquire Spreckels Industries Inc, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Federal Trade Commission approval under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act will allow Columbus McKinnon to buy Spreckels stock for $24 per share.
The cash tender offer is now scheduled to expire at 2400 hr EDT/0400 GMT on October 16, the filing said.

Columbus first filed for approval under the anti-trust improvment act on August 31. The company complied with an October 2 request from the Federal Trade Commission for additional material. The 10-day waiting period expired on October 12.
Columbus McKinnon Corp designs, manufactures and sells a broad range of material handling, lifting and positioning products that are sold in domestic and international markets.
Spreckels is doing business as Yale International Inc.
